extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent prosecutors, IP counsel, corporate IP managers, and other USPTO stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes and analyzes the USPTO's proposed 2017 changes to patent quality measurement, including replacement of the Composite Quality Metric with standardized reviews and new clarity/correctness metrics, and solicits stakeholder comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Quality Metric — final disposition review
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven factors that comprised the USPTO's previous Composite Quality Metric: the final disposition review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically part of a single composite score used to track patent quality on the USPTO dashboard; the Composite Quality Metric combined multiple review types into one number, which the USPTO proposes to discontinue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Quality Metric — in-process review
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven factors that comprised the previous Composite Quality Metric: the in-process review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used previously to identify trends and areas of concern during prosecution; being replaced by new standardized review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Quality Metric — first action on the merits (FAOM) search review
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven factors in the prior Composite Quality Metric: the FAOM search review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured aspects of examiner search quality at first action; the USPTO is consolidating and refining review types under the Master Review Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Quality Metric — complete FAOM review
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven factors in the Composite Quality Metric: the complete FAOM review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed completeness of first-action work product; will be subsumed into the standardized Master Review Form checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Quality Metric — external quality survey
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven factors in the prior Composite Quality Metric: an external quality survey capturing stakeholder opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflected external stakeholder opinions; the USPTO is moving away from a single goal-based score which mixed survey results with work-product measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Quality Metric — internal quality survey
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven Composite Quality Metric factors: an internal quality survey capturing USPTO stakeholder opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the prior composite score methodology that combined survey and process indicators; proposed changes emphasize more direct measures of statutory compliance and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Quality Metric — aggregation of five QIR factors
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the seven factors: an aggregation of five factors from the USPTO's Quality Index Report (QIR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transactional/process indicators from QIR were part of the composite; the new approach intends to use QIR transactional data differently (to identify trends/outliers rather than report a single number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three pillars of patent quality
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO's Enhanced Patent Quality Initiative targets three pillars: (1) excellence in work products, (2) excellence in measuring patent quality, and (3) excellence in customer service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2017 proposed changes focus on the second pillar (measuring patent quality) while supporting the overall initiative to improve examination quality and communication to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work product metric (correctness of actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed core metric representing correctness of actions — a work product metric intended to measure whether examination actions are substantively correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO asked whether focusing on a correctness metric is the right direction; this metric aims to identify improperly made rejections and failures to make rejections where statute requires them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity metric (sufficiency of examiner's reasoning)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed core metric that more thoroughly explores the sufficiency of the examiner's reasoning in an Office Action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to assess whether the rationale in office actions is clearly explained and whether records (e.g., interview recordation) are sufficient; intended to move away from aggregate goal-based scoring toward direct measures of clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling reviews for improperly made rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing a sampling of office actions specifically for improperly made rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the correctness focus: reviewers will check for rejections that were not proper under statute or case law to identify where examiner practice may require improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling reviews for failure to make rejections where statute requires
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing sampled office actions to determine instances where a rejection should have been made but was not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks whether examiners failed to make necessary statutory rejections, identifying under-examination issues as part of correctness measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity review item: whether a rejection was proper
rubrics_metrics.description: A clarity review item example: determining whether a rejection was proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedded within clarity/correctness reviews; pairs substantive correctness with assessment of how well the rejection is explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity review item: whether the statement of the rejection explained the reasons clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: A clarity review item example assessing whether the office action's statement of rejection explained the reasons for the rejection in a clear manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets sufficiency of reasoning/explanation in office actions to improve transparency and allow stakeholders to understand examiners' grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity review item: sufficiency of interview recordation
rubrics_metrics.description: A clarity review item directed to the sufficiency of the recordation of any interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that interview summaries or records adequately reflect discussions and bases for decisions, improving the administrative record and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity review item: propriety of reasons for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: A clarity review item assessing the propriety of any reasons for allowance of an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks whether reasons for allowance are properly justified and documented in the file record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master Review Form — standardized finished product review
rubrics_metrics.description: A single standardized review (the 'Master Review Form') to replace review‑specific forms used in the Composite Quality Metric; to be used by all USPTO reviewers for finished product quality reviews at every stage of prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to provide standardized reviewing criteria (previously different Technology Centers set their own criteria); the draft Master Review Form is available for public viewing and comment as part of the 2017 proposed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of transactional QIR data to identify trends and outliers
rubrics_metrics.description: Using transactional data from the Quality Index Report (QIR) to identify information that can be used to prevent reopening of prosecution, reduce rework, and improve consistency of decision making throughout the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than aggregating QIR indicators into a single score, the proposed approach analyzes transactional data to reveal trends and outlier behavior and to draw attention to potential quality concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move away from single composite score toward targeted metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Public proposal to discontinue the prior Composite Quality Metric (single-reportable number) and instead report metrics that more usefully and transparently reflect quality-related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to improve usefulness and transparency of quality reporting by focusing on concrete measures of statutory compliance and clarity rather than a blended goal-based score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective measurement of clarity and correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO solicits input on how patent metrics can best provide objective, rather than subjective, measurements of quality-related features in clarity and correctness reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders are asked to propose which clarity and correctness review items should drive metrics and how to operationalize them to minimize subjectivity (e.g., explicit checklists, definitional thresholds, or binary yes/no items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional testing and refinement period
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a transitional year (2016) to test and refine the Master Review Form and to optimize QIR data analysis prior to full implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the transition the USPTO will pilot the standardized review, refine wording and procedures, and analyze transactional data to ensure the new metrics function as intended; stakeholders are encouraged to comment before the deadline.
